title: Temporal Regulation of Cell Signaling During Skeletal Myogenesis
content: Skeletal myogenesis proceeds through ordered transitions from muscle stem-cell quiescence to differentiation and fusion. Signal duration, recurrence, and sequence may influence these transitions, but their effects are often confounded by signal quantity and cellular state. Among the studies evaluated, the clearest muscle-specific evidence comes from a circuit linking HES1 (HES family basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor 1), MYOD (myogenic differentiation 1), and DLL1 (delta-like canonical Notch ligand 1). A Dll1 transcriptional-delay allele destabilizes ligand oscillations at near-normal expression, reducing stem-cell maintenance and promoting premature differentiation. Studies of insulin-like growth factor I, extracellular signal-regulated kinases, p38, calcium signaling, and phosphoproteomic trajectories reveal additional temporal structure with different degrees of causal support. A proposed five-level Dynamics-Specific Evidence Ladder distinguishes observation, association, generator perturbation, dynamics-selective perturbation, and controlled waveform replay. Stage-dependent responses and pathway sequence are assessed separately. Waveforms matched for peak activity and integrated exposure can test pattern-dependent causality. Attribution to an individual temporal feature requires additional controls. Aging provides a setting to test mistimed signaling. The framework guides experiments linking signaling history to myogenic fate.
